description: (0.5.0) A retraction of an ancestor accepted (event receipt accepted_at) after T. As of T the event is not admitted; latest admits it. retracted is a caveat, not a refusal (RFC-ACDP-0017 §7.8, §8.1, §10).

did_documents.did:web:registry.example.com: one snapshot observed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z with #receipt-key-1 in verificationMethod

acdp://registry.example.com/aaaaaaaa-aaa.node_verdict: ok_with_caveats (A's own verdict is NOT tainted by B, RFC-ACDP-0017 §8.3)

scenarios.name: B — event with no receipt, attested events required

expected.behavior: Drop event_receipts. As of T the event has no evidence time and is not admitted; since no admitted event follows it, the prefix is empty and retraction is not_retracted. Latest admits the producer-signed event (signature verifies): retracted. Drift retracted_after_as_of.

scenarios.name: C — unreceipted event followed by a receipted one

expected.behavior: Events [retracted, republished (receipt accepted_at < T)]; event_receipts is positional, so position 0 carries a receipt that fails §10.3 (e.g. the one minted for index 1) and is treated as absent: as of T the unadmitted event precedes an admitted one, so retraction is unknown (RFC-ACDP-0017 §7.8 item 3) and the node as-of verdict is unknown.

notes: Behavioral scenarios: the verifier builds the described bundle from real signed bodies, runs verify_chain, and asserts the stage values and verdicts. Test keys: the did:key producer is the sig-001 zero seed (did:key:z6MkiTBz…, not sig-003's 0x42 seed); did:web producer #key-1 is the zero seed and #key-2 is 0x02×32; registry did:web:registry.example.com #receipt-key-1 is 0x11×32. Every bundle whose receipts must verify carries a registry DID snapshot (REG_SNAP) and every producer carries a discovery record unless a scenario removes it. Where present, `vectors` are known answers: the bundle and verdict files plus their pinned digests, executed by scripts/conformance-runner.py (RFC-ACDP-0017 §14).
